question: Which of the following rulers founded the Nalanda University?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kumaragupta I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kumaragupta I**, the ruler of the **Gupta Empire**, established **Nalanda University**, which became an important center of learning in ancient India.
 
• The university was founded during the reign of Kumaragupta I around the **5th century CE**, and it flourished as a renowned center for **Buddhist studies**, philosophy, and other disciplines.
 
• Nalanda University was known for its **residential system of education**, housing over 10,000 students and teachers from different parts of Asia.
 
• The university attracted scholars from countries like **China**, **Tibet**, **Korea**, and **Central Asia**. Famous visitors like **Xuanzang** and **I-Tsing** documented their experiences at Nalanda.
 
• Kumaragupta I was instrumental in laying the foundation of Nalanda University, making it a symbol of the **intellectual and cultural achievements** of the Gupta period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nalanda University:**

 
 
• Located in **Bihar, India**, Nalanda was one of the oldest universities in the world and a major center for **Buddhist education and research**.
 
• The university featured a massive library called the **Dharmaganja**, which housed thousands of manuscripts on various subjects.
 
• Subjects taught included **Buddhist scriptures**, **logic**, **medicine**, **mathematics**, **astronomy**, **philosophy**, and **literature**.
 
• The university was destroyed in the **12th century** by the invasion of **Bakhtiyar Khilji**, marking the end of its glory.
 
 
 
• **Kumaragupta I:**
 
 
• He ruled during the **5th century CE** and was one of the prominent rulers of the **Gupta dynasty**.
 
• Kumaragupta I is remembered for his contributions to cultural and intellectual advancements during his reign.
 
• He issued several **coins and inscriptions**, reflecting the prosperity of the Gupta Empire under his rule.
 
• His reign marked significant developments in **education**, **architecture**, and **religious practices**.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire:**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire, often referred to as the **Golden Age of India**, flourished between the **4th and 6th centuries CE**.
 
• Known for advancements in **science**, **mathematics**, **literature**, **art**, and **architecture**.
 
• Famous scholars such as **Kalidasa**, **Aryabhata**, and **Varahamihira** thrived during this period.
 
• The Gupta rulers were also patrons of **Buddhism**, **Hinduism**, and **Jainism**, contributing to the cultural and religious growth of the empire.
 
 
 
• **Xuanzang and Nalanda:**
 
 
• **Xuanzang**, a Chinese pilgrim and scholar, visited Nalanda University in the **7th century CE**.
 
• He documented the university's **curriculum, administration, and scholarly environment**, providing valuable insights into its functioning.
 
• Xuanzang emphasized the role of Nalanda in spreading **Buddhist teachings** across Asia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other notable Gupta rulers:**

 
 
• **Chandragupta I:** Founder of the Gupta dynasty and instrumental in expanding its territory.
 
• **Samudragupta:** Known as the "Napoleon of India" for his military conquests and patronage of arts.
 
• **Chandragupta II:** Under his reign, India witnessed cultural and economic prosperity, including advancements in trade.
 
 
 
• **Education during Gupta period:**
 
 
• Focus on **higher education** through institutions like **Nalanda** and **Takshashila**.
 
• Subjects ranged from **philosophy**, **astronomy**, and **logic** to **medicine** and **mathematics**.
